notes: Flat body worked on the first attempt exactly as describeCapability's guidance promised — no wrapper trap here, unlike several other tm write capabilities. Top-level response shape matches the declared 201 contract exactly: dataset at the top level (no data envelope), variables returned as an array of {name,uuid} objects (NOT collapsed to a map — no container mismatch), rows as an array of {row_data,row_number,uuid} objects, rows_count (2) agreeing with rows.length. Sent two variables (Browser, OS) with two rows of real, distinct string values (Chrome/Windows, Firefox/MacOS) specifically to exercise the item shape against real data rather than an empty collection — both variables and rows items came back with exactly the declared fields, so the variables/rows item schemas hold under real data, not just structurally-empty responses. The one drift is the same one already registered for the sibling read capability get_dataset: the nested created_by sub-object is declared with id/browserstack_user_id/full_name/email/group_id/onboarded/reports_and_notification_enabled, but the live response instead has id/full_name/email/onboarded/role/reports_and_notification_enabled — browserstack_user_id and group_id are missing, and an undeclared 'role' field is present. This is a real, reproducible schema disagreement (same shape on both the create response and the immediate get_dataset read-back of the same object, see round-trip below), not a one-off. CREATE-then-READ ROUND TRIP (the strong evidence this task asked for): immediately re-read the created dataset via get_dataset(project_id=379335744, uuid=de04f15e-b88a-4409-8b9d-eeff038c3109) — response was byte-identical in shape to the create response (same variables array of {name,uuid}, same rows array of {row_data,row_number,uuid}, same rows_count:2, same created_by shape/drift). The variables container KEPT its declared array shape on both the write response and the independent read — no serializer defect where create returns one container type and a subsequent read returns another. Also queried get_dataset_variables(project_id=379335744, q[name]='Browser') — the project-wide column listing found exactly this dataset's Browser column, with the declared {uuid,name,dataset:{uuid,name,count_rows}} item shape fully intact (count_rows:2, matching the dataset actually written). So across three call sites (create, get_dataset, get_dataset_variables) all touching the same object, the variables/rows containers are consistently arrays with the declared item shape — the only defect present anywhere in this chain is the created_by sub-object drift, which is real but narrow (prose-only fields, not a container-type or entitlement-gate problem). Verdict is DRIFT rather than PASS specifically because of that created_by mismatch, and rather than BLOCKED because the primary create route, its request schema, and its 201 response are all fully functional and correctly documented in every other respect.
